rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Say it once, at its most concrete, then at most one sentence that generalises it. Style, not a gate.
rules_evaluated.evidence: New rule, re-read at current wording this session (`node curriculum/evals/scripts/rule.js writing 27`, dated 2026-08-29). Shape (b), 'a bullet opening with its own `##` header': header at line 12 is 'The file is steady; the agent moves'; the immediately following bullet at line 15 opens 'The file is the steady part; the agent is the moving part' -- a near-verbatim restatement of the header in expanded-sentence form, adding no noun the header lacked, before the same bullet's second clause ('Across all three agents, better rules produce better tickets') adds real, new content. A sibling file (`ae101--exercise--compound-and-close.writing.json`) filed the identical shape non-blocking this session, which calibrates this as a real, low-severity instance of the named pattern rather than overreach. Harm present but small: the restated clause buys the reader nothing past the header one line above it, though the risk of confusion is near zero since it's the SAME claim, not a contradicting one. Counter-reading noted for the maintainer: in a slides-chunked deck (this file renders one `##` per slide), a compressed title expanded into a full sentence as the slide's opening line is also a defensible, common deck convention -- not obviously the corpus-cost the rule is aimed at.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut the opening clause and let the bullet open directly on the generalizing sentence: 'Across all three agents, better rules produce better tickets.' -- or, if the maintainer reads this as legitimate title-expansion for the slide surface, accept-note it so the next judge doesn't re-flag.
